ko.title: [농업학 개론 #13] 수확 후에도 작물은 살아 있습니다 — 그 유지 비법

segments.src: > Harvest is not the finish line. A fruit or vegetable keeps breathing after you pick it, and post-harvest management is the science of slowing that clock so food reaches your plate fresh instead of rotten.
segments.tr: > 수확은 끝이 아닙니다. 과일이나 채소는 수확 후에도 숨을 쉬며, 수확 후 관리는 시계를 늦추어 식품이 썩는 대신 신선하게 식탁에 도달하도록 하는 과학입니다.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 오늘의 개념

segments.src: Here is the fact that surprises most people: a tomato you picked this morning is still a living thing this afternoon.
segments.tr: 대부분의 사람들을 놀라게 하는 사실은 다음과 같습니다. 오늘 아침에 딴 토마토는 오늘 오후에도 여전히 살아 있는 생물입니다.

segments.src: Cut off from the plant, it can no longer refill its water or sugar, but it keeps **respiring** — burning its own stored sugars and giving off heat, carbon dioxide, and water vapor.
segments.tr: 식물에서 잘려 나간 후에는 수나 설탕을 더 이상 보충할 수 없지만, 계속해서 **호흡(respiring)**을 합니다. 즉, 저장된 자체 설탕을 태우며 열, 이산화탄소, 수증기를 내뿜습니다.

segments.src: The faster it breathes, the faster it ages.
segments.tr: 숨을 빨리 쉴수록 더 빨리 늙습니다.

segments.src: Post-harvest management is everything we do between the field and the fork to slow that breathing down.
segments.tr: 수확 후 관리는 그 호흡을 늦추기 위해 밭에서 포크까지 우리가 하는 모든 것입니다.

segments.src: It rests on three pillars.
segments.tr: 여기에는 세 가지 기둥이 있습니다.

segments.src: Harvest at the right maturity.** Pick too early and the produce never develops full flavor or color; pick too late and it's already soft and bruises on the truck.
segments.tr: 알맞은 성숙기에 수확하기.** 너무 일찍 수확하면 농산물이 완전한 풍미나 색상을 발달시키지 못하고, 너무 늦게 수확하면 이미 물러져 트럭 위에서 멍이 듭니다.

segments.src: "Maturity" isn't one thing — a peach for a nearby farmers market can ripen on the tree, but a peach shipping across the country is picked firmer so it finishes ripening on the road.
segments.tr: "성숙기"는 한 가지가 아닙니다. 인근 파머스 마켓용 복숭아는 나무에서 익을 수 있지만, 전국으로 배송되는 복숭아는 유통 과정에서 마저 익도록 더 단단할 때 수확합니다.

segments.src: Sort, grade, and pack.** Right after harvest, produce is cleaned, cooled, and separated by size, color, and quality.
segments.tr: 선별, 등급 분류 및 포장하기.** 수확 직후 농산물은 세척, 냉각되고 크기, 색상, 품질별로 분류됩니다.

segments.src: Damaged items are pulled out — not just because they look bad, but because one moldy berry releases spores and gases that spoil its neighbors.
segments.tr: 손상된 농산물은 단순히 보기 안 좋아서가 아니라 곰팡이 핀 딸기 하나가 주변 농산물을 상하게 하는 포자와 가스를 방출하기 때문에 골라냅니다.

segments.src: ("One bad apple spoils the barrel" is literally true.)
segments.tr: ("썩은 사과 한 개가 통 전체를 망친다"는 말은 문자 그대로 사실입니다.)

segments.src: Good packaging then cushions the produce and controls moisture loss.
segments.tr: 좋은 포장은 농산물을 보호하고 수분 손실을 제어합니다.

segments.src: Store under controlled conditions.** The big three levers are **temperature**, **humidity**, and **air composition**.
segments.tr: 제어된 조건에서 보관하기.** 세 가지 주요 요인은 **온도**, **습도**, **공기 구성**입니다.

segments.src: Cold slows respiration dramatically — as a rule of thumb, every roughly 18°F (10°C) drop can cut the breathing rate by half or more.
segments.tr: 냉장은 호흡을 극적으로 늦춥니다. 경험상 약 18°F(10°C) 떨어질 때마다 호흡률을 절반 이상 줄일 수 있습니다.

segments.src: High humidity keeps produce from wilting as it loses water.
segments.tr: 높은 습도는 농산물이 수분을 잃어 시드는 것을 방지합니다.

segments.src: And in advanced storage, lowering oxygen and raising carbon dioxide (called controlled-atmosphere storage) puts fruit into a kind of hibernation.
segments.tr: 그리고 고급 보관법에서는 산소를 낮추고 이산화탄소를 높여(기밀 저장고라 불림) 과일을 일종의 동면 상태로 만듭니다.

segments.src: One catch: colder is not always better.
segments.tr: 한 가지 함정은 더 차갑다고 항상 좋은 것은 아니라는 점입니다.

segments.src: Tropical crops like bananas, tomatoes, and cucumbers suffer **chilling injury** below about 50°F (10°C) — they get pitted, watery, and off-flavored.
segments.tr: 바나나, 토마토, 오이 같은 열대 작물은 약 50°F(10°C) 이하에서 **저온 장해(chilling injury)**를 입어 구멍이 생기고, 물러지며, 맛이 변합니다.

segments.src: Matching each crop to its own ideal conditions is the whole game.
segments.tr: 각 작물에 맞는 이상적인 조건을 맞추는 것이 핵심입니다.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 일상 생활 속에서

segments.src: Walk into any U.S.
segments.tr: 미국의 아무

segments.src: grocery store and you're standing inside a post-harvest system.
segments.tr: 식료품점에나 들어가면 수확 후 시스템 안에 서 있는 것입니다.

segments.src: The apples in the produce aisle in July were very likely harvested the previous fall in Washington State and held for months in controlled-atmosphere rooms — sealed, chilled, low-oxygen storage that keeps them crisp long after the trees are bare.
segments.tr: 7월 농산물 코너의 사과는 워싱턴주에서 전년도 가을에 수확되어 밀폐되고 냉장된 저산소 저장고인 기밀 저장고에서 몇 달 동안 보관되었을 가능성이 매우 높으며, 나무가 앙상해진 후에도 오랫동안 아삭함을 유지합니다.

segments.src: Notice the details.
segments.tr: 세부 사항을 살펴보세요.

segments.src: The leafy greens sit under a misting sprayer because lettuce is mostly water and wilts fast without high humidity.
segments.tr: 잎채소가 미스트 분사기 아래에 있는 이유는 상추가 대부분 수분으로 이루어져 있어 높은 습도가 없으면 금방 시들기 때문입니다.

segments.src: The bananas are a shelf apart from the apples for a reason: apples give off **ethylene**, a natural ripening gas, and it would turn your green bananas brown ahead of schedule.
segments.tr: 바나나가 사과와 떨어진 진열대에 있는 데는 이유가 있습니다. 사과는 자연 숙성 가스인 **에틸렌**을 방출하여 녹색 바나나를 예정보다 일찍 갈색으로 변하게 만들기 때문입니다.

segments.src: That same ethylene is a kitchen trick — put an unripe avocado in a paper bag with an apple and it ripens in a day or two because the gas gets trapped around it.
segments.tr: 그 동일한 에틸렌은 주방의 팁입니다. 덜 익은 아보카도를 사과와 함께 종이봉투에 넣으면 가스가 주변에 갇히기 때문에 하루 이틀 만에 익습니다.

segments.src: And that whole chilled journey from a California field to a Chicago shelf has a name: the **cold chain**.
segments.tr: 그리고 캘리포니아 농장에서 시카고 진열대까지의 냉장 여정 전체에는 이름이 있습니다. 바로 **콜드 체인(cold chain)**입니다.

segments.src: Every truck, warehouse, and display case is refrigerated so the produce never warms up and restarts its clock.
segments.tr: 모든 트럭, 창고, 진열대는 냉장되어 농산물이 절대 따뜻해져 시계를 다시 시작하지 않도록 합니다.

segments.src: When one link breaks — a truck's cooler fails for a few hours — you see it days later as mushy strawberries.
segments.tr: 하나의 연결고리가 끊어지면—트럭의 냉각기가 몇 시간 동안 고장 나면—며칠 후 딸기가 물러진 것을 보게 됩니다.

segments.src: In the U.S., roughly a third of food is lost or wasted, and a big share of the produce portion traces back to breaks in exactly this chain.
segments.tr: 미국에서는 식량의 약 3분의 1이 손실되거나 낭비되며, 농산물 부분의 상당수는 정확히 이 체인의 단절로 거슬러 올라갑니다.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 세 줄 요약

segments.src: - Produce stays alive and keeps respiring after harvest, so the goal is to slow that metabolism, not just to store it.
segments.tr: - 농산물은 수확 후에도 살아 있어 계속 호흡하므로, 단순히 보관하는 것이 아니라 신진대사를 늦추는 것이 목표입니다.

segments.src: - The core levers are harvest timing, careful sorting and packing, and control of temperature, humidity, and air composition.
segments.tr: - 핵심 요인은 수확 시기, 신중한 선별 및 포장, 온도, 습도, 공기 구성 제어입니다.

segments.src: - Cold slows aging but tropical crops suffer chilling injury, and an unbroken cold chain is what carries quality from farm to shelf.
segments.tr: - 저온은 노화를 늦추지만 열대 작물은 저온 장해를 입으며, 끊기지 않는 콜드 체인이 농장에서 진열대까지 품질을 전달합니다.

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 셀프 퀴즈

segments.src: 1. Why does chilling most produce extend its shelf life?
segments.tr: 1. 대부분의 농산물을 냉장 보관하면 유통기한이 연장되는 이유는 무엇인가요?

segments.src: - A) It kills all bacteria instantly
segments.tr: - A) 모든 박테리아를 즉시 죽이기 때문

segments.src: - B) It slows the produce's respiration rate
segments.tr: - B) 농산물의 호흡률을 늦추기 때문

segments.src: - C) It adds water back into the fruit
segments.tr: - C) 과일에 수분을 다시 공급하기 때문

segments.src: - D) It increases the sugar content
segments.tr: - D) 당도를 높이기 때문

segments.src: 2. True or False: Storing bananas right next to apples helps the bananas stay green longer.
segments.tr: 2. O 또는 X: 바나나를 사과 바로 옆에 보관하면 바나나를 더 오랫동안 초록빛으로 유지하는 데 도움이 된다.

segments.src: 3. Which crop is MOST likely to suffer chilling injury in a very cold refrigerator?
segments.tr: 3. 아주 차가운 냉장고에서 저온 장해를 입을 가능성이 **가장 높은** 작물은 무엇인가요?

segments.src: - A) Apple
segments.tr: - A) 사과

segments.src: - B) Carrot
segments.tr: - B) 당근

segments.src: - C) Tomato
segments.tr: - C) 토마토

segments.src: - D) Cabbage
segments.tr: - D) 양배추

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 오늘의 용어

segments.src: - **Respiration:** The process by which harvested produce burns its stored sugars, giving off heat, CO2, and water — the main driver of aging after picking.
segments.tr: - **호흡(Respiration):** 수확한 농산물이 저장된 당분을 태우며 열, CO2, 수분을 방출하는 과정 — 수확 후 노화를 유발하는 주원인입니다.

segments.src: - **Cold chain:** An unbroken series of refrigerated steps (harvest, transport, storage, display) that keeps produce cold from farm to consumer.
segments.tr: - **콜드 체인(Cold chain):** 농장에서 소비자까지 농산물을 차갑게 유지하기 위해 냉장 단계(수확, 운송, 보관, 진열)가 끊김 없이 이어지는 과정입니다.

segments.src: - **Ethylene:** A natural plant gas that triggers ripening; useful for ripening on purpose but harmful when it over-ripens nearby produce.
segments.tr: - **에틸렌(Ethylene):** 숙성을 유발하는 천연 식물 가스; 의도적인 숙성에는 유용하지만 주변 농산물을 과숙성시킬 때는 해롭습니다.

segments.src: - **Chilling injury:** Damage to warm-climate crops stored too cold (below about 50°F/10°C), showing up as pitting, watery spots, and off-flavors.
segments.tr: - **저온 장해(Chilling injury):** 너무 차갑게(약 50°F/10°C 이하) 보관된 온대·열대 기후 작물의 손상으로, 구멍, 물집, 이취로 나타납니다.

segments.src: - **Controlled-atmosphere storage:** Storage that lowers oxygen and raises carbon dioxide to slow ripening, letting crops like apples keep for months.
segments.tr: - **기밀 저장고(Controlled-atmosphere storage):** 산소를 낮추고 이산화탄소를 높여 숙성을 늦추고 사과 같은 작물이 몇 달 동안 보관되도록 하는 저장고입니다.

segments.src: *Answers: 1) B — cold slows the respiration rate, so the produce ages and breaks down more slowly (it does not sterilize or rehydrate the food).
segments.tr: *정답: 1) B — 저온은 호흡률을 늦추어 농산물이 더 천천히 늙고 분해되도록 합니다(식품을 살균하거나 수분을 재공급하는 것은 아닙니다).

segments.src: 2) False — apples release ethylene, which speeds ripening and turns bananas brown faster, so keep them apart.
segments.tr: 2) X — 사과는 숙성을 촉진하고 바나나를 더 빨리 갈색으로 만드는 에틸렌을 방출하므로 따로 보관해야 합니다.

segments.src: 3) C — the tomato is a warm-climate crop prone to chilling injury; apples, carrots, and cabbage tolerate near-freezing storage well.*
segments.tr: 3) C — 토마토는 저온 장해에 취약한 따뜻한 기후 작물입니다. 사과, 당근, 양배추는 빙점 가까운 보관을 잘 견뎌냅니다.*

zh.title: [农业 101 #13] 收获后的农产品依然“活着”——我们如何保持其新鲜度

segments.src: > Harvest is not the finish line. A fruit or vegetable keeps breathing after you pick it, and post-harvest management is the science of slowing that clock so food reaches your plate fresh instead of rotten.
segments.tr: > 收获并不是终点。水果或蔬菜在采摘后仍在呼吸，而采后管理就是通过科学手段减缓这一过程，让食物在到达餐桌时依然新鲜，而不是腐烂。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日概念

segments.src: Here is the fact that surprises most people: a tomato you picked this morning is still a living thing this afternoon.
segments.tr: 有一个事实让大多数人感到惊讶：你今天早上采摘的番茄，到了下午依然是一个活体。

segments.src: Cut off from the plant, it can no longer refill its water or sugar, but it keeps **respiring** — burning its own stored sugars and giving off heat, carbon dioxide, and water vapor.
segments.tr: 脱离植株后，它无法再补充水分或糖分，但它仍在持续进行**呼吸作用**——消耗自身储存的糖分，并释放热量、二氧化碳和水蒸气。

segments.src: The faster it breathes, the faster it ages.
segments.tr: 呼吸越快，衰老越快。

segments.src: Post-harvest management is everything we do between the field and the fork to slow that breathing down.
segments.tr: 采后管理就是我们在田间到餐桌之间所做的一切，旨在减缓这种呼吸作用。

segments.src: It rests on three pillars.
segments.tr: 它建立在三大支柱之上。

segments.src: Harvest at the right maturity.** Pick too early and the produce never develops full flavor or color; pick too late and it's already soft and bruises on the truck.
segments.tr: 适时采收。** 采收过早，农产品无法发育出完整的风味或色泽；采收过晚，它已经变软，在运输车上就会被压伤。

segments.src: "Maturity" isn't one thing — a peach for a nearby farmers market can ripen on the tree, but a peach shipping across the country is picked firmer so it finishes ripening on the road.
segments.tr: “成熟度”并非单一标准——供应附近农贸市场的桃子可以在树上自然成熟，但要运往全国各地的桃子则会采摘得更硬一些，以便在运输途中完成成熟过程。

segments.src: Sort, grade, and pack.** Right after harvest, produce is cleaned, cooled, and separated by size, color, and quality.
segments.tr: 分拣、分级和包装。** 收获后，农产品会立即进行清洁、冷却，并按大小、颜色和质量进行分类。

segments.src: Damaged items are pulled out — not just because they look bad, but because one moldy berry releases spores and gases that spoil its neighbors.
segments.tr: 受损的产品会被挑出来——这不仅是因为它们看起来不好，还因为一个发霉的浆果会释放孢子和气体，导致周围的农产品变质。

segments.src: ("One bad apple spoils the barrel" is literally true.)
segments.tr: （“一颗老鼠屎坏了一锅粥”在这里是字面意义上的真理。）

segments.src: Good packaging then cushions the produce and controls moisture loss.
segments.tr: 良好的包装可以缓冲农产品并控制水分流失。

segments.src: Store under controlled conditions.** The big three levers are **temperature**, **humidity**, and **air composition**.
segments.tr: 在受控条件下储存。** 三大核心杠杆是**温度**、**湿度**和**空气成分**。

segments.src: Cold slows respiration dramatically — as a rule of thumb, every roughly 18°F (10°C) drop can cut the breathing rate by half or more.
segments.tr: 低温能显著减缓呼吸作用——经验法则是，温度每降低约 18°F (10°C)，呼吸速率通常会降低一半甚至更多。

segments.src: High humidity keeps produce from wilting as it loses water.
segments.tr: 高湿度可以防止农产品因水分流失而萎蔫。

segments.src: And in advanced storage, lowering oxygen and raising carbon dioxide (called controlled-atmosphere storage) puts fruit into a kind of hibernation.
segments.tr: 在先进的储存技术中，降低氧气含量并提高二氧化碳含量（称为气调储存）能让水果进入一种“冬眠”状态。

segments.src: One catch: colder is not always better.
segments.tr: 有一个问题：越冷并不总是越好。

segments.src: Tropical crops like bananas, tomatoes, and cucumbers suffer **chilling injury** below about 50°F (10°C) — they get pitted, watery, and off-flavored.
segments.tr: 香蕉、番茄和黄瓜等热带作物在低于约 50°F (10°C) 的环境下会遭受**冷害**——它们会出现凹陷、水渍和风味变差。

segments.src: Matching each crop to its own ideal conditions is the whole game.
segments.tr: 为每种作物匹配其理想的储存条件是整个过程的关键。

segments.tr: ## 日常生活中的应用

segments.src: Walk into any U.S.
segments.tr: 走进任何一家美国

segments.src: grocery store and you're standing inside a post-harvest system.
segments.tr: 杂货店，你其实就站在一个采后管理系统之中。

segments.src: The apples in the produce aisle in July were very likely harvested the previous fall in Washington State and held for months in controlled-atmosphere rooms — sealed, chilled, low-oxygen storage that keeps them crisp long after the trees are bare.
segments.tr: 7 月份在农产品货架上看到的苹果，很可能是在前一年秋天于华盛顿州收获的，并在气调库中储存了数月——这种密封、冷藏、低氧的储存环境，让它们在树木早已落叶后依然保持清脆。

segments.src: Notice the details.
segments.tr: 注意观察细节。

segments.src: The leafy greens sit under a misting sprayer because lettuce is mostly water and wilts fast without high humidity.
segments.tr: 绿叶蔬菜放在喷雾器下，因为生菜大部分是水，如果没有高湿度，很快就会萎蔫。

segments.src: The bananas are a shelf apart from the apples for a reason: apples give off **ethylene**, a natural ripening gas, and it would turn your green bananas brown ahead of schedule.
segments.tr: 香蕉与苹果分开摆放是有原因的：苹果会释放**乙烯**（一种天然催熟气体），这会让你绿色的香蕉提前变黄变褐。

segments.src: That same ethylene is a kitchen trick — put an unripe avocado in a paper bag with an apple and it ripens in a day or two because the gas gets trapped around it.
segments.tr: 同样的乙烯也是一种厨房小技巧——把未成熟的牛油果和苹果一起放进纸袋里，它一两天内就会成熟，因为气体被困在了周围。

segments.src: And that whole chilled journey from a California field to a Chicago shelf has a name: the **cold chain**.
segments.tr: 从加州田间到芝加哥货架的整个冷藏旅程有一个名字：**冷链**。

segments.src: Every truck, warehouse, and display case is refrigerated so the produce never warms up and restarts its clock.
segments.tr: 每一辆卡车、仓库和展示柜都经过冷藏，以确保农产品永远不会升温并重新启动其衰老时钟。

segments.src: When one link breaks — a truck's cooler fails for a few hours — you see it days later as mushy strawberries.
segments.tr: 当其中一个环节断裂——比如卡车的冷却器坏了几个小时——你几天后就会看到软烂的草莓。

segments.src: In the U.S., roughly a third of food is lost or wasted, and a big share of the produce portion traces back to breaks in exactly this chain.
segments.tr: 在美国，大约三分之一的食物被浪费或损耗，而很大一部分农产品的浪费正是源于这一链条的断裂。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 三行总结

segments.src: - Produce stays alive and keeps respiring after harvest, so the goal is to slow that metabolism, not just to store it.
segments.tr: - 农产品在收获后依然活着并持续呼吸，因此目标是减缓其代谢，而不仅仅是储存。

segments.src: - The core levers are harvest timing, careful sorting and packing, and control of temperature, humidity, and air composition.
segments.tr: - 核心杠杆包括收获时机、精细的分拣包装，以及对温度、湿度和空气成分的控制。

segments.src: - Cold slows aging but tropical crops suffer chilling injury, and an unbroken cold chain is what carries quality from farm to shelf.
segments.tr: - 低温能减缓衰老，但热带作物会遭受冷害，而完整的冷链是确保品质从农场传递到货架的关键。

segments.src: ## ✅ Self-Quiz
segments.tr: ## ✅ 自测题

segments.src: 1. Why does chilling most produce extend its shelf life?
segments.tr: 1. 为什么冷藏大多数农产品能延长其保质期？

segments.src: - A) It kills all bacteria instantly
segments.tr: - A) 它能瞬间杀死所有细菌

segments.src: - B) It slows the produce's respiration rate
segments.tr: - B) 它减缓了农产品的呼吸速率

segments.src: - C) It adds water back into the fruit
segments.tr: - C) 它能为水果补充水分

segments.src: - D) It increases the sugar content
segments.tr: - D) 它增加了含糖量

segments.src: 2. True or False: Storing bananas right next to apples helps the bananas stay green longer.
segments.tr: 2. 对或错：把香蕉和苹果放在一起储存有助于香蕉保持绿色更久。

segments.src: 3. Which crop is MOST likely to suffer chilling injury in a very cold refrigerator?
segments.tr: 3. 在非常冷的冰箱中，哪种作物最容易遭受冷害？

segments.src: - A) Apple
segments.tr: - A) 苹果

segments.src: - B) Carrot
segments.tr: - B) 胡萝卜

segments.src: - C) Tomato
segments.tr: - C) 番茄

segments.src: - D) Cabbage
segments.tr: - D) 卷心菜

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日术语

segments.src: - **Respiration:** The process by which harvested produce burns its stored sugars, giving off heat, CO2, and water — the main driver of aging after picking.
segments.tr: - **呼吸作用 (Respiration)：** 收获后的农产品消耗其储存的糖分，释放热量、二氧化碳和水分的过程——这是采摘后衰老的主要驱动力。

segments.src: - **Cold chain:** An unbroken series of refrigerated steps (harvest, transport, storage, display) that keeps produce cold from farm to consumer.
segments.tr: - **冷链 (Cold chain)：** 一系列不间断的冷藏环节（收获、运输、储存、展示），使农产品从农场到消费者手中始终保持低温。

segments.src: - **Ethylene:** A natural plant gas that triggers ripening; useful for ripening on purpose but harmful when it over-ripens nearby produce.
segments.tr: - **乙烯 (Ethylene)：** 一种触发成熟的天然植物气体；用于人工催熟很有用，但当它导致附近农产品过熟时则有害。

segments.src: - **Chilling injury:** Damage to warm-climate crops stored too cold (below about 50°F/10°C), showing up as pitting, watery spots, and off-flavors.
segments.tr: - **冷害 (Chilling injury)：** 温暖气候作物在储存温度过低（低于约 50°F/10°C）时受到的损害，表现为凹陷、水渍和风味变差。

segments.src: - **Controlled-atmosphere storage:** Storage that lowers oxygen and raises carbon dioxide to slow ripening, letting crops like apples keep for months.
segments.tr: - **气调储存 (Controlled-atmosphere storage)：** 通过降低氧气和提高二氧化碳含量来减缓成熟的储存方式，使苹果等作物能保存数月。

segments.src: *Answers: 1) B — cold slows the respiration rate, so the produce ages and breaks down more slowly (it does not sterilize or rehydrate the food).
segments.tr: *答案：1) B — 低温减缓了呼吸速率，因此农产品衰老和分解得更慢（它不能消毒或为食物补水）。

segments.src: 2) False — apples release ethylene, which speeds ripening and turns bananas brown faster, so keep them apart.
segments.tr: 2) 错 — 苹果释放乙烯，这会加速成熟并使香蕉更快变褐，所以要将它们分开。

segments.src: 3) C — the tomato is a warm-climate crop prone to chilling injury; apples, carrots, and cabbage tolerate near-freezing storage well.*
segments.tr: 3) C — 番茄是温暖气候作物，容易遭受冷害；苹果、胡萝卜和卷心菜可以很好地耐受接近冰点的储存环境。*

hi.title: [Agriculture 101 #13] फसल कटाई के बाद भी जीवित रहती है — जानिए हम ऐसा कैसे बनाए रखते हैं

segments.src: > Harvest is not the finish line. A fruit or vegetable keeps breathing after you pick it, and post-harvest management is the science of slowing that clock so food reaches your plate fresh instead of rotten.
segments.tr: > कटाई अंतिम चरण नहीं है। फसल काटने के बाद भी फल या सब्ज़ी सांस लेती रहती है, और कटाई के बाद का प्रबंधन (पोस्ट-हार्वेस्ट मैनेजमेंट) उस घड़ी को धीमा करने का विज्ञान है ताकि भोजन सड़ने के बजाय ताज़ा आपकी थाली तक पहुँचे।

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## आज की अवधारणा

segments.src: Here is the fact that surprises most people: a tomato you picked this morning is still a living thing this afternoon.
segments.tr: यहाँ वह तथ्य है जो अधिकांश लोगों को चकित करता है: आज सुबह आपके द्वारा तोड़ा गया टमाटर आज दोपहर भी एक जीवित चीज़ है।

segments.src: Cut off from the plant, it can no longer refill its water or sugar, but it keeps **respiring** — burning its own stored sugars and giving off heat, carbon dioxide, and water vapor.
segments.tr: पौधे से अलग होने के बाद, यह अब अपने पानी या शर्करा को दोबारा नहीं भर सकता है, लेकिन यह **सांस लेता** रहता है — अपनी संचित शर्करा को जलाता है और गर्मी, कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड तथा जल वाष्प छोड़ता है।

segments.src: The faster it breathes, the faster it ages.
segments.tr: यह जितनी तेज़ी से सांस लेगा, उतनी ही तेज़ी से पुराना होगा।

segments.src: Post-harvest management is everything we do between the field and the fork to slow that breathing down.
segments.tr: कटाई के बाद का प्रबंधन वह सब कुछ है जो हम खेत से लेकर थाली तक उस सांस लेने की प्रक्रिया को धीमा करने के लिए करते हैं।

segments.src: It rests on three pillars.
segments.tr: यह तीन स्तंभों पर आधारित है।

segments.src: Harvest at the right maturity.** Pick too early and the produce never develops full flavor or color; pick too late and it's already soft and bruises on the truck.
segments.tr: सही परिपक्वता पर कटाई करें।** बहुत जल्दी काट लें तो उपज कभी भी पूरा स्वाद या रंग विकसित नहीं कर पाती; बहुत देर से काट लें तो यह पहले से ही नरम हो जाती है और ट्रक पर कुचल जाती है।

segments.src: "Maturity" isn't one thing — a peach for a nearby farmers market can ripen on the tree, but a peach shipping across the country is picked firmer so it finishes ripening on the road.
segments.tr: "परिपक्वता" कोई एक चीज़ नहीं है — पास के किसानों के बाज़ार के लिए एक आड़ू पेड़ पर पक सकता है, लेकिन देश भर में भेजा जाने वाला आड़ू अधिक सख्त तोड़ा जाता है ताकि वह रास्ते में पकना पूरा कर सके।

segments.src: Sort, grade, and pack.** Right after harvest, produce is cleaned, cooled, and separated by size, color, and quality.
segments.tr: छाँटें, ग्रेड करें और पैक करें।** कटाई के तुरंत बाद, उपज को साफ किया जाता है, ठंडा किया जाता है, और आकार, रंग तथा गुणवत्ता के आधार पर अलग किया जाता है।

segments.src: Damaged items are pulled out — not just because they look bad, but because one moldy berry releases spores and gases that spoil its neighbors.
segments.tr: क्षतिग्रस्त वस्तुओं को बाहर निकाल दिया जाता है — इसलिए नहीं कि वे खराब दिखती हैं, बल्कि इसलिए कि एक फफूंदयुक्त बेरी ऐसे बीजाणु और गैसें छोड़ती है जो उसके पड़ोसियों को खराब कर देती हैं।

segments.src: ("One bad apple spoils the barrel" is literally true.)
segments.tr: ("एक सड़ा हुआ सेब पूरे बैरल को खराब कर देता है" यह बिल्कुल सच है।)

segments.src: Good packaging then cushions the produce and controls moisture loss.
segments.tr: अच्छी पैकेजिंग तब उपज को कुशन करती है और नमी की हानि को नियंत्रित करती है।

segments.src: Store under controlled conditions.** The big three levers are **temperature**, **humidity**, and **air composition**.
segments.tr: नियंत्रित परिस्थितियों में स्टोर करें।** तीन बड़े लीवर **तापमान**, **आर्द्रता**, और **हवा की संरचना** हैं।

segments.src: Cold slows respiration dramatically — as a rule of thumb, every roughly 18°F (10°C) drop can cut the breathing rate by half or more.
segments.tr: ठंड श्वसन को नाटकीय रूप से धीमा कर देती है — अंगूठे के नियम के रूप में, लगभग हर 18°F (10°C) की गिरावट सांस लेने की दर को आधा या उससे अधिक कम कर सकती है।

segments.src: High humidity keeps produce from wilting as it loses water.
segments.tr: उच्च आर्द्रता उपज को पानी खोने पर मुरझाने से रोकती है।

segments.src: And in advanced storage, lowering oxygen and raising carbon dioxide (called controlled-atmosphere storage) puts fruit into a kind of hibernation.
segments.tr: और उन्नत भंडारण में, ऑक्सीजन कम करना और कार्बन डाइऑक्साइड बढ़ाना (जिसे नियंत्रित-वातावरण भंडारण कहा जाता है) फल को एक प्रकार की हाइबरनेशन में डाल देता है।

segments.src: One catch: colder is not always better.
segments.tr: एक पेंच: ठंडा होना हमेशा बेहतर नहीं होता है।

segments.src: Tropical crops like bananas, tomatoes, and cucumbers suffer **chilling injury** below about 50°F (10°C) — they get pitted, watery, and off-flavored.
segments.tr: केले, टमाटर और ककड़ी जैसी उष्णकटिबंधीय फसलें लगभग 50°F (10°C) से नीचे **चिलिंग इंजरी** (ठंड से होने वाली क्षति) से पीड़ित होती हैं — वे गड्ढेदार, पानीदार और बेस्वाद हो जाती हैं।

segments.src: Matching each crop to its own ideal conditions is the whole game.
segments.tr: प्रत्येक फसल को उसकी अपनी आदर्श परिस्थितियों से मिलाना ही पूरा खेल है।

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## रोज़मर्रा की ज़िंदगी में

segments.tr: अमेरिका के किसी भी

segments.src: The apples in the produce aisle in July were very likely harvested the previous fall in Washington State and held for months in controlled-atmosphere rooms — sealed, chilled, low-oxygen storage that keeps them crisp long after the trees are bare.
segments.tr: जुलाई में उपज गलियारे में सेब बहुत संभव है कि वाशिंगटन राज्य में पिछली शरद ऋतु में काटे गए थे और नियंत्रित-वातावरण के कमरों में महीनों तक रखे गए थे — सील, ठंडे, कम ऑक्सीजन वाले भंडारण जो पेड़ों के नंगे होने के लंबे समय बाद भी उन्हें कुरकुरा रखते हैं।

segments.tr: विवरणों पर ध्यान दें।

segments.tr: पत्तेदार साग एक मिस्टिंग स्प्रेयर के नीचे बैठते हैं क्योंकि सलाद पत्ता ज्यादातर पानी है और उच्च आर्द्रता के बिना तेजी से मुरझा जाता है।

segments.tr: केले सेब से एक शेल्फ दूर एक कारण से हैं: सेब **एथिलीन** छोड़ते हैं, जो एक प्राकृतिक पकने वाली गैस है, और यह समय से पहले आपके हरे केलों को भूरा कर देगा।

segments.src: That same ethylene is a kitchen trick — put an unripe avocado in a paper bag with an apple and it ripens in a day or two because the gas gets trapped around it.
segments.tr: वही एथिलीन एक रसोई की चाल है — एक सेब के साथ एक कागज के थैले में एक कच्चे एवोकैडो को रखें और यह एक या दो दिन में पक जाता है क्योंकि गैस इसके चारों ओर फंस जाती है।

segments.src: And that whole chilled journey from a California field to a Chicago shelf has a name: the **cold chain**.
segments.tr: और कैलिफोर्निया के खेत से शिकागो के शेल्फ तक की उस पूरी ठंडी यात्रा का एक नाम है: **कोल्ड चेन**।

segments.src: Every truck, warehouse, and display case is refrigerated so the produce never warms up and restarts its clock.
segments.tr: हर ट्रक, गोदाम, और डिस्प्ले केस को प्रशीतनित किया जाता है ताकि उपज कभी गर्म न हो और अपनी घड़ी को पुनरारंभ न करे।

segments.src: When one link breaks — a truck's cooler fails for a few hours — you see it days later as mushy strawberries.
segments.tr: जब एक कड़ी टूटती है — एक ट्रक का कूलर कुछ घंटों के लिए विफल हो जाता है — तो आप इसे दिनों बाद mushy स्ट्रॉबेरी के रूप में देखते हैं।

segments.src: In the U.S., roughly a third of food is lost or wasted, and a big share of the produce portion traces back to breaks in exactly this chain.
segments.tr: अमेरिका में, लगभग एक तिहाई भोजन खो जाता है या बर्बाद हो जाता है, और उपज के हिस्से का एक बड़ा हिस्सा बिल्कुल इसी श्रृंखला में टूटता है।

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## तीन-पंक्ति रीकैप

segments.tr: - उपज जीवित रहती है और कटाई के बाद सांस लेती रहती है, इसलिए लक्ष्य उस चयापचय को धीमा करना है, न कि केवल इसे स्टोर करना।

es.title: [Agriculture 101 #13] El cultivo sigue vivo después de la cosecha: así es como lo mantenemos así

segments.src: > Harvest is not the finish line. A fruit or vegetable keeps breathing after you pick it, and post-harvest management is the science of slowing that clock so food reaches your plate fresh instead of rotten.
segments.tr: > La cosecha no es la línea de meta. Una fruta o verdura sigue respirando después de cosecharla, y la gestión postcosecha es la ciencia de ralentizar ese reloj para que los alimentos lleguen a su plato frescos en lugar de podridos.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## El concepto de hoy

segments.src: Here is the fact that surprises most people: a tomato you picked this morning is still a living thing this afternoon.
segments.tr: Aquí está el hecho que sorprende a la mayoría de las personas: un tomate que recolectó esta mañana sigue siendo un ser vivo esta tarde.

segments.src: Cut off from the plant, it can no longer refill its water or sugar, but it keeps **respiring** — burning its own stored sugars and giving off heat, carbon dioxide, and water vapor.
segments.tr: Separado de la planta, ya no puede reponer su agua o azúcar, pero sigue **respirando**: quema sus propios azúcares almacenados y emite calor, dióxido de carbono y vapor de agua.

segments.src: The faster it breathes, the faster it ages.
segments.tr: Cuanto más rápido respira, más rápido envejece.

segments.src: Post-harvest management is everything we do between the field and the fork to slow that breathing down.
segments.tr: La gestión postcosecha es todo lo que hacemos entre el campo y el tenedor para ralentizar esa respiración.

segments.src: It rests on three pillars.
segments.tr: Se sustenta en tres pilares.

segments.src: Harvest at the right maturity.** Pick too early and the produce never develops full flavor or color; pick too late and it's already soft and bruises on the truck.
segments.tr: Cosechar en el momento de madurez adecuado.** Si se recolecta demasiado pronto, el producto nunca desarrolla todo su sabor o color; si se recolecta demasiado tarde, ya está blando y se golpea en el camión.

segments.src: "Maturity" isn't one thing — a peach for a nearby farmers market can ripen on the tree, but a peach shipping across the country is picked firmer so it finishes ripening on the road.
segments.tr: La "madurez" no es una sola cosa: un durazno para un mercado de agricultores cercano puede madurar en el árbol, pero un durazno que se envía a través del país se recolecta más firme para que termine de madurar en el camino.

segments.src: Sort, grade, and pack.** Right after harvest, produce is cleaned, cooled, and separated by size, color, and quality.
segments.tr: Clasificar, calibrar y empacar.** Justo después de la cosecha, el producto se limpia, se enfría y se separa por tamaño, color y calidad.

segments.src: Damaged items are pulled out — not just because they look bad, but because one moldy berry releases spores and gases that spoil its neighbors.
segments.tr: Los artículos dañados se retiran, no solo porque se ven mal, sino porque una baya mohosa libera esporas y gases que estropean a sus vecinas.

segments.src: ("One bad apple spoils the barrel" is literally true.)
segments.tr: ("Una manzana podrida echa a perder el barril" es literalmente verdad).

segments.src: Good packaging then cushions the produce and controls moisture loss.
segments.tr: Un buen empaque luego amortigua el producto y controla la pérdida de humedad.

segments.src: Store under controlled conditions.** The big three levers are **temperature**, **humidity**, and **air composition**.
segments.tr: Almacenar en condiciones controladas.** Las tres grandes palancas son la **temperatura**, la **humedad** y la **composición del aire**.

segments.src: Cold slows respiration dramatically — as a rule of thumb, every roughly 18°F (10°C) drop can cut the breathing rate by half or more.
segments.tr: El frío ralentiza la respiración drásticamente; como regla general, cada caída de aproximadamente 18°F (10°C) puede reducir la tasa de respiración a la mitad o más.

segments.src: High humidity keeps produce from wilting as it loses water.
segments.tr: La alta humedad evita que los productos se marchiten al perder agua.

segments.src: And in advanced storage, lowering oxygen and raising carbon dioxide (called controlled-atmosphere storage) puts fruit into a kind of hibernation.
segments.tr: Y en el almacenamiento avanzado, reducir el oxígeno y aumentar el dióxido de carbono (llamado almacenamiento en atmósfera controlada) pone a la fruta en una especie de hibernación.

segments.src: One catch: colder is not always better.
segments.tr: Un detalle: más frío no siempre es mejor.

segments.src: Tropical crops like bananas, tomatoes, and cucumbers suffer **chilling injury** below about 50°F (10°C) — they get pitted, watery, and off-flavored.
segments.tr: Los cultivos tropicales como los plátanos, los tomates y los pepinos sufren **daños por frío** por debajo de los 50°F (10°C); se vuelven picados, aguados y con sabores extraños.

segments.src: Matching each crop to its own ideal conditions is the whole game.
segments.tr: Adaptar cada cultivo a sus propias condiciones ideales es todo el juego.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## En la vida cotidiana

segments.src: Walk into any U.S.
segments.tr: Entre a cualquier

segments.src: grocery store and you're standing inside a post-harvest system.
segments.tr: supermercado de EE. UU. y estará parado dentro de un sistema postcosecha.

segments.src: The apples in the produce aisle in July were very likely harvested the previous fall in Washington State and held for months in controlled-atmosphere rooms — sealed, chilled, low-oxygen storage that keeps them crisp long after the trees are bare.
segments.tr: Las manzanas en el pasillo de productos agrícolas en julio muy probablemente fueron cosechadas el otoño anterior en el estado de Washington y se mantuvieron durante meses en salas de atmósfera controlada: almacenamiento sellado, refrigerado y bajo en oxígeno que las mantiene crujientes mucho después de que los árboles están desprovistos de hojas.

segments.src: Notice the details.
segments.tr: Observe los detalles.

segments.src: The leafy greens sit under a misting sprayer because lettuce is mostly water and wilts fast without high humidity.
segments.tr: Las verduras de hoja verde se sientan bajo un rociador de niebla porque la lechuga es principalmente agua y se marchita rápido sin alta humedad.

segments.src: The bananas are a shelf apart from the apples for a reason: apples give off **ethylene**, a natural ripening gas, and it would turn your green bananas brown ahead of schedule.
segments.tr: Los plátanos están en un estante separado de las manzanas por una razón: las manzanas emiten **etileno**, un gas de maduración natural, y eso volvería marrones sus plátanos verdes antes de tiempo.

segments.src: That same ethylene is a kitchen trick — put an unripe avocado in a paper bag with an apple and it ripens in a day or two because the gas gets trapped around it.
segments.tr: Ese mismo etileno es un truco de cocina: ponga un aguacate verde en una bolsa de papel con una manzana y madurará en uno o dos días porque el gas queda atrapado a su alrededor.

segments.src: And that whole chilled journey from a California field to a Chicago shelf has a name: the **cold chain**.
segments.tr: Y todo ese viaje refrigerado desde un campo de California hasta el estante de Chicago tiene un nombre: la **cadena de frío**.

segments.src: Every truck, warehouse, and display case is refrigerated so the produce never warms up and restarts its clock.
segments.tr: Cada camión, almacén y vitrina está refrigerado para que el producto nunca se caliente y reinicie su reloj.

segments.src: When one link breaks — a truck's cooler fails for a few hours — you see it days later as mushy strawberries.
segments.tr: Cuando un eslabón se rompe (el enfriador de un camión falla durante unas horas), lo ves días después en forma de fresas blandas.

segments.src: In the U.S., roughly a third of food is lost or wasted, and a big share of the produce portion traces back to breaks in exactly this chain.
segments.tr: En EE. UU., aproximadamente un tercio de los alimentos se pierden o se desperdician, y una gran parte de la porción de productos agrícolas se remonta a rupturas en exactamente esta cadena.

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## Resumen de tres líneas

segments.src: - Produce stays alive and keeps respiring after harvest, so the goal is to slow that metabolism, not just to store it.
segments.tr: - Los productos agrícolas se mantienen vivos y siguen respirando después de la cosecha, por lo que el objetivo es ralentizar ese metabolismo, no solo almacenarlos.

segments.src: - The core levers are harvest timing, careful sorting and packing, and control of temperature, humidity, and air composition.
segments.tr: - Las palancas principales son el momento de la cosecha, la clasificación y el empaque cuidadosos, y el control de la temperatura, la humedad y la composición del aire.

segments.src: - Cold slows aging but tropical crops suffer chilling injury, and an unbroken cold chain is what carries quality from farm to shelf.
segments.tr: - El frío ralentiza el envejecimiento, pero los cultivos tropicales sufren daños por frío, y una cadena de frío ininterrumpida es lo que transporta la calidad desde la granja hasta el estante.

segments.src: - **Respiration:** The process by which harvested produce burns its stored sugars, giving off heat, CO2, and water — the main driver of aging after picking.

fr.title: [Agriculture 101 #13] Le fruit est vivant après la récolte — Voici comment nous maintenons cet état

segments.src: > Harvest is not the finish line. A fruit or vegetable keeps breathing after you pick it, and post-harvest management is the science of slowing that clock so food reaches your plate fresh instead of rotten.
segments.tr: > La récolte n'est pas la ligne d'arrivée. Un fruit ou un légume continue de respirer après sa cueillette, et la gestion post-récolte est la science qui consiste à ralentir cette horloge pour que la nourriture arrive fraîche dans votre assiette plutôt que pourrie.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Le concept d'aujourd'hui

segments.src: Here is the fact that surprises most people: a tomato you picked this morning is still a living thing this afternoon.
segments.tr: Voici le fait qui surprend la plupart des gens : une tomate cueillie ce matin est encore un être vivant cet après-midi.

segments.src: Cut off from the plant, it can no longer refill its water or sugar, but it keeps **respiring** — burning its own stored sugars and giving off heat, carbon dioxide, and water vapor.
segments.tr: Coupée de la plante, elle ne peut plus reconstituer son eau ni son sucre, mais elle continue de **respirer** — en brûlant ses propres sucres stockés et en dégageant de la chaleur, du dioxyde de carbone et de la vapeur d'eau.

segments.src: The faster it breathes, the faster it ages.
segments.tr: Plus elle respire vite, plus elle vieillit rapidement.

segments.src: Post-harvest management is everything we do between the field and the fork to slow that breathing down.
segments.tr: La gestion post-récolte englobe tout ce que nous faisons entre le champ et la fourchette pour ralentir cette respiration.

segments.src: It rests on three pillars.
segments.tr: Elle repose sur trois piliers.

segments.src: Harvest at the right maturity.** Pick too early and the produce never develops full flavor or color; pick too late and it's already soft and bruises on the truck.
segments.tr: Récolter au bon degré de maturité.** Cueillir trop tôt empêche le produit de développer toute sa saveur ou sa couleur ; cueillir trop tard le rend déjà mou et sujet aux bleus sur le camion.

segments.src: "Maturity" isn't one thing — a peach for a nearby farmers market can ripen on the tree, but a peach shipping across the country is picked firmer so it finishes ripening on the road.
segments.tr: "La maturité" n'est pas une notion unique : une pêche destinée à un marché de producteurs local peut mûrir sur l'arbre, mais une pêche expédiée à l'autre bout du pays est cueillie plus ferme pour finir de mûrir en route.

segments.src: Sort, grade, and pack.** Right after harvest, produce is cleaned, cooled, and separated by size, color, and quality.
segments.tr: Trier, classer et emballer.** Juste après la récolte, les produits sont nettoyés, refroidis et séparés selon leur taille, leur couleur et leur qualité.

segments.src: Damaged items are pulled out — not just because they look bad, but because one moldy berry releases spores and gases that spoil its neighbors.
segments.tr: Les articles endommagés sont retirés — non seulement parce qu'ils ont mauvaise apparence, mais parce qu'une seule baie moisie libère des spores et des gaz qui gâtent ses voisines.

segments.src: ("One bad apple spoils the barrel" is literally true.)
segments.tr: ("Une seule pomme gâte le panier" est littéralement vrai.)

segments.src: Good packaging then cushions the produce and controls moisture loss.
segments.tr: Un bon emballage protège ensuite les produits et limite la perte d'humidité.

segments.src: Store under controlled conditions.** The big three levers are **temperature**, **humidity**, and **air composition**.
segments.tr: Conserver dans des conditions contrôlées.** Les trois grands leviers sont la **température**, l'**humidité** et la **composition de l'air**.

segments.src: Cold slows respiration dramatically — as a rule of thumb, every roughly 18°F (10°C) drop can cut the breathing rate by half or more.
segments.tr: Le froid ralentit considérablement la respiration : en règle générale, chaque baisse d'environ 18°F (10°C) peut réduire le taux de respiration de moitié ou plus.

segments.src: High humidity keeps produce from wilting as it loses water.
segments.tr: Une humidité élevée empêche les produits de se flétrir en perdant de l'eau.

segments.src: And in advanced storage, lowering oxygen and raising carbon dioxide (called controlled-atmosphere storage) puts fruit into a kind of hibernation.
segments.tr: Et dans le stockage avancé, abaisser l'oxygène et augmenter le dioxyde de carbone (ce que l'on appelle l'atmosphère contrôlée) plonge les fruits dans une sorte d'hibernation.

segments.src: One catch: colder is not always better.
segments.tr: Un piège : plus froid n'est pas toujours mieux.

segments.src: Tropical crops like bananas, tomatoes, and cucumbers suffer **chilling injury** below about 50°F (10°C) — they get pitted, watery, and off-flavored.
segments.tr: Les cultures tropicales comme les bananes, les tomates et les concombres subissent des **dommages dus au froid** en dessous d'environ 50°F (10°C) — ils se piquent, deviennent aqueux et perdent leur saveur.

segments.src: Matching each crop to its own ideal conditions is the whole game.
segments.tr: Adapter chaque culture à ses conditions idéales est tout l'enjeu.

pt.title: [Agriculture 101 #13] O Produto Continua Vivo Após a Colheita — Aqui está Como Mantemos Dessa Forma

segments.src: > Harvest is not the finish line. A fruit or vegetable keeps breathing after you pick it, and post-harvest management is the science of slowing that clock so food reaches your plate fresh instead of rotten.
segments.tr: > A colheita não é a linha de chegada. Uma fruta ou vegetação continua respirando depois que você a colhe, e o manejo pós-colheita é a ciência de desacelerar esse relógio para que o alimento chegue ao seu prato fresco em vez de apodrecido.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## O Conceito de Hoje

segments.src: Here is the fact that surprises most people: a tomato you picked this morning is still a living thing this afternoon.
segments.tr: Aqui está o fato que surpreende a maioria das pessoas: um tomate que você colheu esta manhã ainda é um ser vivo esta tarde.

segments.src: Cut off from the plant, it can no longer refill its water or sugar, but it keeps **respiring** — burning its own stored sugars and giving off heat, carbon dioxide, and water vapor.
segments.tr: Cortado da planta, não pode mais reabastecer sua água ou açúcar, mas continua **respirando** — queimando seus próprios açúcares armazenados e liberando calor, dióxido de carbono e vapor de água.

segments.src: The faster it breathes, the faster it ages.
segments.tr: Quanto mais rápido respira, mais rápido envelhece.

segments.src: Post-harvest management is everything we do between the field and the fork to slow that breathing down.
segments.tr: O manejo pós-colheita é tudo que fazemos entre o campo e o garfo para desacelerar essa respiração.

segments.src: It rests on three pillars.
segments.tr: Repousa em três pilares.

segments.src: Harvest at the right maturity.** Pick too early and the produce never develops full flavor or color; pick too late and it's already soft and bruises on the truck.
segments.tr: Colha na maturidade certa.** Colha muito cedo e o produto nunca desenvolve sabor ou cor completos; colha muito tarde e já está macio e com hematomas no caminhão.

segments.src: "Maturity" isn't one thing — a peach for a nearby farmers market can ripen on the tree, but a peach shipping across the country is picked firmer so it finishes ripening on the road.
segments.tr: "Maturidade" não é uma coisa — um pêssego para um mercado de agricultores próximo pode amadurecer na árvore, mas um pêssego que viaja pelo país é colhido mais firme para terminar de amadurecer no caminho.

segments.src: Sort, grade, and pack.** Right after harvest, produce is cleaned, cooled, and separated by size, color, and quality.
segments.tr: Ordene, classifique e empacote.** Logo após a colheita, o produto é limpo, resfriado e separado por tamanho, cor e qualidade.

segments.src: Damaged items are pulled out — not just because they look bad, but because one moldy berry releases spores and gases that spoil its neighbors.
segments.tr: Itens danificados são removidos — não apenas porque parecem ruins, mas porque uma baga mofada libera esporos e gases que prejudicam seus vizinhos.

segments.src: ("One bad apple spoils the barrel" is literally true.)
segments.tr: ("Uma maçã podre estraga o barril" é literalmente verdadeiro.)

segments.src: Good packaging then cushions the produce and controls moisture loss.
segments.tr: Uma boa embalagem então amortece o produto e controla a perda de umidade.

segments.src: Store under controlled conditions.** The big three levers are **temperature**, **humidity**, and **air composition**.
segments.tr: Armazene sob condições controladas.** Os três grandes controles são **temperatura**, **umidade** e **composição do ar**.

segments.src: Cold slows respiration dramatically — as a rule of thumb, every roughly 18°F (10°C) drop can cut the breathing rate by half or more.
segments.tr: O frio desacelera a respiração dramaticamente — como regra de ouro, uma queda de aproximadamente 18°F (10°C) pode reduzir a taxa de respiração em até metade ou mais.

segments.src: High humidity keeps produce from wilting as it loses water.
segments.tr: A alta umidade evita que o produto murche enquanto perde água.

segments.src: And in advanced storage, lowering oxygen and raising carbon dioxide (called controlled-atmosphere storage) puts fruit into a kind of hibernation.
segments.tr: E no armazenamento avançado, reduzir oxigênio e aumentar dióxido de carbono (chamado armazenamento de atmosfera controlada) coloca a fruta em uma espécie de hibernação.

segments.src: One catch: colder is not always better.
segments.tr: Uma ressalva: mais frio nem sempre é melhor.

segments.src: Tropical crops like bananas, tomatoes, and cucumbers suffer **chilling injury** below about 50°F (10°C) — they get pitted, watery, and off-flavored.
segments.tr: Culturas tropicais como bananas, tomates e pepinos sofrem **lesão de frio** abaixo de aproximadamente 50°F (10°C) — ficam marcadas, aquosas e com sabor alterado.

segments.src: Matching each crop to its own ideal conditions is the whole game.
segments.tr: Adaptar cada cultura às suas próprias condições ideais é o jogo todo.

segments.tr: Esse mesmo etileno é um truque de cozinha — coloque um abacate imaturo em um saco de papel com uma maçã e amadurece em um ou dois dias porque o gás fica preso ao seu redor.

segments.src: And that whole chilled journey from a California field to a Chicago shelf has a name: the **cold chain**.
segments.tr: E essa jornada inteira refrigerada de um campo da Califórnia para uma prateleira de Chicago tem um nome: a **cadeia fria**.

segments.src: Every truck, warehouse, and display case is refrigerated so the produce never warms up and restarts its clock.
segments.tr: Cada caminhão, armazém e vitrine é refrigerada para que o produto nunca aqueça e reinicie seu relógio.

segments.src: When one link breaks — a truck's cooler fails for a few hours — you see it days later as mushy strawberries.
segments.tr: Quando um elo se quebra — o resfriador de um caminhão falha por algumas horas — você vê isso dias depois como morangos moles.

segments.src: In the U.S., roughly a third of food is lost or wasted, and a big share of the produce portion traces back to breaks in exactly this chain.
segments.tr: Nos EUA, aproximadamente um terço dos alimentos é perdido ou desperdiçado, e uma grande parcela da perda de produtos remonta a quebras exatamente nesta cadeia.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Termos de Hoje

segments.src: - **Respiration:** The process by which harvested produce burns its stored sugars, giving off heat, CO2, and water — the main driver of aging after picking.
segments.tr: - **Respiração:** O processo pelo qual o produto colhido queima seus açúcares armazenados, liberando calor, CO2 e água — o principal motor do envelhecimento após a colheita.

segments.src: - **Cold chain:** An unbroken series of refrigerated steps (harvest, transport, storage, display) that keeps produce cold from farm to consumer.
segments.tr: - **Cadeia fria:** Uma série ininterrupta de etapas refrigeradas (colheita, transporte, armazenamento, exibição) que mantém o produto frio da fazenda ao consumidor.

segments.src: - **Ethylene:** A natural plant gas that triggers ripening; useful for ripening on purpose but harmful when it over-ripens nearby produce.
segments.tr: - **Etileno:** Um gás de planta natural que desencadeia o amadurecimento; útil para amadurecer propositalmente, mas prejudicial quando amadurece excessivamente os produtos próximos.

segments.src: - **Chilling injury:** Damage to warm-climate crops stored too cold (below about 50°F/10°C), showing up as pitting, watery spots, and off-flavors.
segments.tr: - **Lesão de frio:** Dano às culturas de clima quente armazenadas muito frias (abaixo de aproximadamente 50°F/10°C), aparecendo como depressões, manchas aquosas e sabores alterados.

segments.src: - **Controlled-atmosphere storage:** Storage that lowers oxygen and raises carbon dioxide to slow ripening, letting crops like apples keep for months.
segments.tr: - **Armazenamento de atmosfera controlada:** Armazenamento que reduz oxigênio e aumenta dióxido de carbono para desacelerar o amadurecimento, permitindo que culturas como maçãs durem meses.

segments.src: *Answers: 1) B — cold slows the respiration rate, so the produce ages and breaks down more slowly (it does not sterilize or rehydrate the food).
segments.tr: *Respostas: 1) B — o frio desacelera a taxa de respiração, então o produto envelhece e se decompõe mais lentamente (não esteriliza nem reidrata o alimento).

segments.src: 2) False — apples release ethylene, which speeds ripening and turns bananas brown faster, so keep them apart.
segments.tr: 2) Falso — as maçãs liberam etileno, que acelera o amadurecimento e torna as bananas marrom mais rápido, então mantenha-as separadas.

segments.src: 3) C — the tomato is a warm-climate crop prone to chilling injury; apples, carrots, and cabbage tolerate near-freezing storage well.*
segments.tr: 3) C — o tomate é uma cultura de clima quente propensa a lesão de frio; maçãs, cenouras e repolho toleram bem o armazenamento próximo ao congelamento.*

segments.src: - **Ethylene:** A natural plant gas that triggers ripening; useful for ripening on purpose but harmful when it over-ripens nearby produce.

segments.src: - **Chilling injury:** Damage to warm-climate crops stored too cold (below about 50°F/10°C), showing up as pitting, watery spots, and off-flavors.
segments.tr: - **Cedera akibat pendinginan:** Kerusakan pada tanaman iklim hangat yang disimpan terlalu dingin (di bawah sekitar 50°F/10°C), muncul sebagai lubang, bintik berair, dan rasa tidak enak.

segments.src: - **Controlled-atmosphere storage:** Storage that lowers oxygen and raises carbon dioxide to slow ripening, letting crops like apples keep for months.
segments.tr: - **Penyimpanan atmosfer terkontrol:** Penyimpanan yang menurunkan oksigen dan menaikkan karbon dioksida untuk memperlambat pelematangan, memungkinkan tanaman seperti apel bertahan berbulan-bulan.

segments.src: 2) False — apples release ethylene, which speeds ripening and turns bananas brown faster, so keep them apart.
segments.tr: 2) Salah — apel melepaskan etilen, yang mempercepat pelematangan dan mengubah pisang menjadi cokelat lebih cepat, jadi pisahkan mereka.

segments.src: 3) C — the tomato is a warm-climate crop prone to chilling injury; apples, carrots, and cabbage tolerate near-freezing storage well.*

ja.title: [農業101 #13] 作物は収穫後も生きている — 新鮮に保つ方法

segments.src: > Harvest is not the finish line. A fruit or vegetable keeps breathing after you pick it, and post-harvest management is the science of slowing that clock so food reaches your plate fresh instead of rotten.
segments.tr: > 収穫はゴールではない。摘んだ後も、果物や野菜は呼吸を続ける。収穫後の管理とは、その時計を遅くして、腐ったものではなく新鮮な食べ物があなたの食卓に届くようにするための科学である。

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## 今日のコンセプト

segments.src: Here is the fact that surprises most people: a tomato you picked this morning is still a living thing this afternoon.
segments.tr: ほとんどの人を驚かせる事実がここにある：今朝摘んだトマトは、午後になってもまだ生きている。

segments.src: Cut off from the plant, it can no longer refill its water or sugar, but it keeps **respiring** — burning its own stored sugars and giving off heat, carbon dioxide, and water vapor.
segments.tr: 植物から切り離されると、水や糖分を補給できなくなるが、それでも**呼吸を続ける** — 貯蔵された糖分を燃やし、熱、二酸化炭素、水蒸気を放出する。

segments.src: The faster it breathes, the faster it ages.
segments.tr: 呼吸が速いほど、老化も速い。

segments.src: Post-harvest management is everything we do between the field and the fork to slow that breathing down.
segments.tr: 収穫後の管理とは、農場から食卓までの間で、その呼吸を遅くするために行うすべてのことである。

segments.src: It rests on three pillars.
segments.tr: それは3つの柱に支えられている。

segments.src: Harvest at the right maturity.** Pick too early and the produce never develops full flavor or color; pick too late and it's already soft and bruises on the truck.
segments.tr: 適切な成熟度で収穫する。** 早く摘みすぎると、農産物は十分な風味や色を発展させず、遅く摘みすぎると、既に柔らかく、輸送中に傷がつく。

segments.src: "Maturity" isn't one thing — a peach for a nearby farmers market can ripen on the tree, but a peach shipping across the country is picked firmer so it finishes ripening on the road.
segments.tr: 「成熟度」は単一ではない — 近くの農場市場向けの桃は木の上で熟すことができるが、国内を横断して出荷される桃はより硬く摘まれ、輸送中に熟成を完了する。

segments.src: Sort, grade, and pack.** Right after harvest, produce is cleaned, cooled, and separated by size, color, and quality.
segments.tr: 選別、等級分け、梱包する。** 収穫直後、農産物は洗浄され、冷却され、サイズ、色、品質で分類される。

segments.src: Damaged items are pulled out — not just because they look bad, but because one moldy berry releases spores and gases that spoil its neighbors.
segments.tr: 傷のある品目は取り除かれる — 見た目が悪いからだけではなく、1つのカビたベリーが胞子とガスを放出して、その周辺の品目を台無しにするからである。

segments.src: ("One bad apple spoils the barrel" is literally true.)
segments.tr: （「腐ったリンゴ1つが樽全体を台無しにする」という言葉は文字通り真実である。）

segments.src: Good packaging then cushions the produce and controls moisture loss.
segments.tr: 良好な梱包は農産物にクッション性を与え、水分損失を制御する。

segments.src: Store under controlled conditions.** The big three levers are **temperature**, **humidity**, and **air composition**.
segments.tr: 管理された条件下で保管する。** 3つの主な要素は、**温度**、**湿度**、**空気組成**である。

segments.src: Cold slows respiration dramatically — as a rule of thumb, every roughly 18°F (10°C) drop can cut the breathing rate by half or more.
segments.tr: 冷却は呼吸を劇的に遅くする — 経験則として、約18°F (10°C) の低下ごとに、呼吸速度を半分以上削減できる。

segments.src: High humidity keeps produce from wilting as it loses water.
segments.tr: 高湿度は、農産物が水分を失う際にしおれるのを防ぐ。

segments.src: And in advanced storage, lowering oxygen and raising carbon dioxide (called controlled-atmosphere storage) puts fruit into a kind of hibernation.
segments.tr: 高度な保管では、酸素を低下させ、二酸化炭素を上昇させることで（制御大気貯蔵と呼ばれる）、果実を一種の冬眠状態に置く。

segments.src: One catch: colder is not always better.
segments.tr: ただし注意点がある：より冷たいことが常に良いわけではない。

segments.src: Tropical crops like bananas, tomatoes, and cucumbers suffer **chilling injury** below about 50°F (10°C) — they get pitted, watery, and off-flavored.
segments.tr: バナナ、トマト、キュウリなどの熱帯作物は、約50°F (10°C) 以下で**冷害**を受ける — 陥没し、水っぽく、風味が悪くなる。

segments.src: Matching each crop to its own ideal conditions is the whole game.
segments.tr: 各作物を独自の理想的な条件に合わせることが全てである。

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## 日常生活で

segments.src: Walk into any U.S.
segments.tr: 任意の米国の

segments.src: grocery store and you're standing inside a post-harvest system.
segments.tr: 食料品店に入ると、あなたは収穫後システムの内部に立っている。

segments.src: The apples in the produce aisle in July were very likely harvested the previous fall in Washington State and held for months in controlled-atmosphere rooms — sealed, chilled, low-oxygen storage that keeps them crisp long after the trees are bare.
segments.tr: 7月の青果売り場のリンゴは、前年の秋にワシントン州で収穫され、管理大気室で数ヶ月間保管された可能性が高い — 密閉され、冷却され、低酸素貯蔵で、木が裸になった後も長期間シャキシャキの状態を保つ。

segments.src: Notice the details.
segments.tr: 細部に注意を払ってほしい。

segments.src: The leafy greens sit under a misting sprayer because lettuce is mostly water and wilts fast without high humidity.
segments.tr: 葉物野菜はミスティングスプレーの下に置かれている。レタスはほぼ水分からなり、高湿度がないと素早くしおれるからである。

segments.src: The bananas are a shelf apart from the apples for a reason: apples give off **ethylene**, a natural ripening gas, and it would turn your green bananas brown ahead of schedule.
segments.tr: バナナがリンゴから別の棚に置かれているのには理由がある：リンゴは**エチレン**という天然の熟成ガスを放出し、それは緑色のバナナを予定より早く茶色に変えてしまう。

segments.src: That same ethylene is a kitchen trick — put an unripe avocado in a paper bag with an apple and it ripens in a day or two because the gas gets trapped around it.
segments.tr: その同じエチレンは台所のコツである — 熟していないアボカドを紙袋に入れ、リンゴと一緒に置くと、ガスがその周辺に閉じ込められるため、1～2日で熟する。

segments.src: And that whole chilled journey from a California field to a Chicago shelf has a name: the **cold chain**.
segments.tr: そして、カリフォルニアの畑からシカゴの棚までの全体的な冷却された旅には名前がある：**コールドチェーン**。

segments.src: Every truck, warehouse, and display case is refrigerated so the produce never warms up and restarts its clock.
segments.tr: すべてのトラック、倉庫、および陳列ケースは冷蔵され、農産物は温まらず、時間を再開しない。

segments.src: When one link breaks — a truck's cooler fails for a few hours — you see it days later as mushy strawberries.
segments.tr: 1つのリンクが破断する場合 — トラックのクーラーが数時間故障する — 数日後、それがドロドロのイチゴとして見られる。

segments.src: In the U.S., roughly a third of food is lost or wasted, and a big share of the produce portion traces back to breaks in exactly this chain.
segments.tr: 米国では、約3分の1の食料が失われたり廃棄されたりし、農産物の大部分がこのチェーンの破断に遡る。

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap
segments.tr: ## 3行のまとめ

segments.src: - Produce stays alive and keeps respiring after harvest, so the goal is to slow that metabolism, not just to store it.
segments.tr: - 農産物は収穫後も生きており、呼吸し続けるため、目標は単に保管することではなく、その代謝を遅くすることである。

segments.src: - The core levers are harvest timing, careful sorting and packing, and control of temperature, humidity, and air composition.
segments.tr: - 主要な要素は、収穫タイミング、慎重な選別と梱包、および温度、湿度、空気組成の制御である。

segments.src: - Cold slows aging but tropical crops suffer chilling injury, and an unbroken cold chain is what carries quality from farm to shelf.
segments.tr: - 冷却は老化を遅くするが、熱帯作物は冷害を受け、切断されないコールドチェーンが農場から棚に品質を運ぶ。

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 今日の用語

segments.src: - **Respiration:** The process by which harvested produce burns its stored sugars, giving off heat, CO2, and water — the main driver of aging after picking.
segments.tr: - **呼吸：** 収穫された農産物が貯蔵された糖分を燃やし、熱、CO2、および水を放出するプロセス — 摘み取り後の老化の主な原因。

segments.src: - **Cold chain:** An unbroken series of refrigerated steps (harvest, transport, storage, display) that keeps produce cold from farm to consumer.
segments.tr: - **コールドチェーン：** 農場から消費者まで農産物を冷却のままにする、切断されない冷蔵ステップのシリーズ（収穫、輸送、保管、展示）。

segments.src: - **Ethylene:** A natural plant gas that triggers ripening; useful for ripening on purpose but harmful when it over-ripens nearby produce.
segments.tr: - **エチレン：** 熟成を引き起こす天然植物ガス；目的のために熟成させるのに役立つが、近くの農産物を過度に熟成させる場合は有害である。

segments.src: - **Chilling injury:** Damage to warm-climate crops stored too cold (below about 50°F/10°C), showing up as pitting, watery spots, and off-flavors.
segments.tr: - **冷害：** 温暖気候作物に対する損傷で、あまりにも冷たく保管される（約50°F/10°C以下）、陥没、水っぽい斑点、および風味の悪さとして現れる。

segments.src: - **Controlled-atmosphere storage:** Storage that lowers oxygen and raises carbon dioxide to slow ripening, letting crops like apples keep for months.
segments.tr: - **制御大気貯蔵：** 酸素を低下させ、二酸化炭素を上昇させて熟成を遅くし、リンゴなどの作物を数ヶ月間保つことを可能にする貯蔵。

segments.src: *Answers: 1) B — cold slows the respiration rate, so the produce ages and breaks down more slowly (it does not sterilize or rehydrate the food).
segments.tr: *回答：1) B — 冷却は呼吸速度を遅くするため、農産物はより緩やかに老化し、崩壊する（食べ物を滅菌したり、再水和したりしない）。

segments.src: 2) False — apples release ethylene, which speeds ripening and turns bananas brown faster, so keep them apart.
segments.tr: 2) 偽 — リンゴはエチレンを放出し、それは熟成を加速させ、バナナをより速く茶色に変えるため、分けて保つこと。

segments.src: 3) C — the tomato is a warm-climate crop prone to chilling injury; apples, carrots, and cabbage tolerate near-freezing storage well.*
segments.tr: 3) C — トマトは冷害を受けやすい温暖気候作物である；リンゴ、ニンジン、キャベツは氷点近くの保管を十分に許容する。*

segments.src: ## Three-Line Recap

segments.src: - Produce stays alive and keeps respiring after harvest, so the goal is to slow that metabolism, not just to store it.
segments.tr: - Produkte bleiben lebendig und atmen weiterhin nach der Ernte, daher ist das Ziel, diesen Stoffwechsel zu verlangsamen, nicht nur sie zu lagern.

segments.src: - The core levers are harvest timing, careful sorting and packing, and control of temperature, humidity, and air composition.
segments.tr: - Die Kernhebel sind Erntezeit, sorgfältige Sortierung und Verpackung sowie Kontrolle von Temperatur, Luftfeuchtigkeit und Luftzusammensetzung.

segments.src: - Cold slows aging but tropical crops suffer chilling injury, and an unbroken cold chain is what carries quality from farm to shelf.
segments.tr: - Kälte verlangsamt das Altern, aber tropische Kulturen leiden unter Kälteschäden, und eine ununterbrochene Kühlkette ist das, was Qualität vom Feld zum Regal bringt.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Heutige Begriffe

segments.src: - **Respiration:** The process by which harvested produce burns its stored sugars, giving off heat, CO2, and water — the main driver of aging after picking.
segments.tr: - **Atmung:** Der Prozess, durch den geerntete Produkte ihre gespeicherten Zucker verbrennen, Wärme, CO2 und Wasserdampf abgeben — der Haupttreiber des Alterns nach dem Pflücken.

segments.src: - **Cold chain:** An unbroken series of refrigerated steps (harvest, transport, storage, display) that keeps produce cold from farm to consumer.
segments.tr: - **Kühlkette:** Eine ununterbrochene Reihe von gekühlten Schritten (Ernte, Transport, Lagerung, Verkauf), die Produkte vom Hof bis zum Verbraucher kühl hält.

segments.src: - **Ethylene:** A natural plant gas that triggers ripening; useful for ripening on purpose but harmful when it over-ripens nearby produce.
segments.tr: - **Ethylen:** Ein natürliches Pflanzengas, das Reifung auslöst; nützlich für absichtliche Reifung, aber schädlich, wenn es nahegelegene Produkte überreift.

segments.src: - **Chilling injury:** Damage to warm-climate crops stored too cold (below about 50°F/10°C), showing up as pitting, watery spots, and off-flavors.
segments.tr: - **Kälteschaden:** Schaden an Warmklima-Kulturen, die zu kalt gelagert werden (unter etwa 50°F/10°C), mit Dellen, wässrigen Flecken und geschmacklichen Beeinträchtigungen.

segments.src: - **Controlled-atmosphere storage:** Storage that lowers oxygen and raises carbon dioxide to slow ripening, letting crops like apples keep for months.
segments.tr: - **Lagerung mit kontrollierter Atmosphäre:** Lagerung, die Sauerstoff senkt und Kohlendioxid erhöht, um Reifung zu verlangsamen, so dass Kulturen wie Äpfel monatelang frisch bleiben.

segments.src: *Answers: 1) B — cold slows the respiration rate, so the produce ages and breaks down more slowly (it does not sterilize or rehydrate the food).
segments.tr: *Antworten: 1) B — Kälte verlangsamt die Atmungsrate, so dass Produkte langsamer altern und sich abbauen (es sterilisiert oder rehydriert das Lebensmittel nicht).

segments.src: 2) False — apples release ethylene, which speeds ripening and turns bananas brown faster, so keep them apart.
segments.tr: 2) Falsch — Äpfel geben Ethylen ab, das Reifung beschleunigt und Bananen schneller braun werden lässt, also halten Sie sie getrennt.

segments.src: 3) C — the tomato is a warm-climate crop prone to chilling injury; apples, carrots, and cabbage tolerate near-freezing storage well.*
segments.tr: 3) C — die Tomate ist eine Warmklima-Kultur, die anfällig für Kälteschäden ist; Äpfel, Karotten und Kohl vertragen eine Lagerung in der Nähe von Gefriertemperaturen gut.*

vi.title: [Nông Nghiệp 101 #13] Sản Phẩm Vẫn Sống Sau Khi Thu Hoạch — Cách Chúng Tôi Bảo Quản Nó

segments.src: > Harvest is not the finish line. A fruit or vegetable keeps breathing after you pick it, and post-harvest management is the science of slowing that clock so food reaches your plate fresh instead of rotten.
segments.tr: > Thu hoạch không phải là đích đến. Trái cây hoặc rau quả vẫn tiếp tục hô hấp sau khi bạn hái nó, và quản lý sau thu hoạch là khoa học giảm chậm quá trình này để thực phẩm đến bàn ăn của bạn tươi thay vì thối.

segments.src: ## Today's Concept
segments.tr: ## Khái Niệm Hôm Nay

segments.src: Here is the fact that surprises most people: a tomato you picked this morning is still a living thing this afternoon.
segments.tr: Đây là sự thật khiến hầu hết mọi người ngạc nhiên: quả cà chua bạn hái sáng nay vẫn còn là một sinh vật sống vào chiều nay.

segments.src: Cut off from the plant, it can no longer refill its water or sugar, but it keeps **respiring** — burning its own stored sugars and giving off heat, carbon dioxide, and water vapor.
segments.tr: Bị cắt khỏi cây, nó không thể nạp lại nước hoặc đường, nhưng nó tiếp tục **hô hấp** — đốt cháy đường lưu trữ của riêng nó và tỏa ra nhiệt, carbon dioxide, và hơi nước.

segments.src: The faster it breathes, the faster it ages.
segments.tr: Nó hô hấp càng nhanh, nó lão hóa càng nhanh.

segments.src: Post-harvest management is everything we do between the field and the fork to slow that breathing down.
segments.tr: Quản lý sau thu hoạch là tất cả những gì chúng tôi làm giữa cánh đồng và chiếc nĩa để làm chậm hô hấp đó.

segments.src: It rests on three pillars.
segments.tr: Nó dựa trên ba trụ cột.

segments.src: Harvest at the right maturity.** Pick too early and the produce never develops full flavor or color; pick too late and it's already soft and bruises on the truck.
segments.tr: Thu hoạch ở độ chín thích hợp.** Hái quá sớm và sản phẩm không bao giờ phát triển hương vị hoặc màu sắc đầy đủ; hái quá muộn và nó đã mềm và bị bầm tím trên xe.

segments.src: "Maturity" isn't one thing — a peach for a nearby farmers market can ripen on the tree, but a peach shipping across the country is picked firmer so it finishes ripening on the road.
segments.tr: "Độ chín" không phải là một thứ — một quả đào cho chợ nông dân gần đó có thể chín trên cây, nhưng quả đào vận chuyển khắp quốc gia được hái cứng hơn để nó hoàn thành chín trên đường.

segments.src: Sort, grade, and pack.** Right after harvest, produce is cleaned, cooled, and separated by size, color, and quality.
segments.tr: Phân loại, xếp hạng và đóng gói.** Ngay sau khi thu hoạch, sản phẩm được làm sạch, làm lạnh và phân tách theo kích thước, màu sắc và chất lượng.

segments.src: Damaged items are pulled out — not just because they look bad, but because one moldy berry releases spores and gases that spoil its neighbors.
segments.tr: Những sản phẩm bị hỏng được loại bỏ — không chỉ vì chúng trông xấu, mà vì một quả mọng bị mốc phát thải bào tử và khí làm hỏng những sản phẩm xung quanh.

segments.src: ("One bad apple spoils the barrel" is literally true.)
segments.tr: ("Một quả táo xấu làm hỏng cả thùng" là đúng theo đúng nghĩa.)

segments.src: Good packaging then cushions the produce and controls moisture loss.
segments.tr: Đóng gói tốt sau đó bảo vệ sản phẩm và kiểm soát mất ẩm.

segments.src: Store under controlled conditions.** The big three levers are **temperature**, **humidity**, and **air composition**.
segments.tr: Lưu trữ dưới các điều kiện kiểm soát.** Ba đòn bẩy chính là **nhiệt độ**, **độ ẩm**, và **thành phần không khí**.

segments.src: Cold slows respiration dramatically — as a rule of thumb, every roughly 18°F (10°C) drop can cut the breathing rate by half or more.
segments.tr: Lạnh làm chậm hô hấp đáng kể — theo nguyên tắc chung, mỗi sự giảm khoảng 18°F (10°C) có thể cắt giảm tốc độ hô hấp xuống một nửa hoặc hơn.

segments.src: High humidity keeps produce from wilting as it loses water.
segments.tr: Độ ẩm cao giữ sản phẩm không héo khi nó mất nước.

segments.src: And in advanced storage, lowering oxygen and raising carbon dioxide (called controlled-atmosphere storage) puts fruit into a kind of hibernation.
segments.tr: Và trong kho lưu trữ tiên tiến, giảm oxy và tăng carbon dioxide (gọi là kho lưu trữ với khí quyển kiểm soát) đưa trái cây vào một loại ngủ đông.

segments.src: One catch: colder is not always better.
segments.tr: Một điều cần chú ý: lạnh hơn không phải lúc nào cũng tốt hơn.

segments.src: Tropical crops like bananas, tomatoes, and cucumbers suffer **chilling injury** below about 50°F (10°C) — they get pitted, watery, and off-flavored.
segments.tr: Cây trồng nhiệt đới như chuối, cà chua và dưa chuột bị **tổn thương do lạnh** dưới khoảng 50°F (10°C) — chúng bị chỏm lõm, ướt nhũn và mất hương vị.

segments.src: Matching each crop to its own ideal conditions is the whole game.
segments.tr: Phù hợp mỗi cây trồng với điều kiện lý tưởng của riêng nó là toàn bộ trò chơi.

segments.src: ## In Everyday Life
segments.tr: ## Trong Cuộc Sống Hàng Ngày

segments.src: Walk into any U.S.
segments.tr: Bước vào bất kỳ cửa hàng Hoa Kỳ

segments.src: grocery store and you're standing inside a post-harvest system.
segments.tr: và bạn đang đứng bên trong một hệ thống sau thu hoạch.

segments.src: The apples in the produce aisle in July were very likely harvested the previous fall in Washington State and held for months in controlled-atmosphere rooms — sealed, chilled, low-oxygen storage that keeps them crisp long after the trees are bare.
segments.tr: Những quả táo trong khu sản phẩm tươi vào tháng 7 rất có thể được thu hoạch vào mùa thu năm trước ở Washington State và được giữ trong nhiều tháng trong các phòng có khí quyển kiểm soát — lưu trữ kín, lạnh, oxy thấp giữ chúng giòn lâu sau khi cây trơi lá.

segments.src: Notice the details.
segments.tr: Chú ý đến các chi tiết.

segments.src: The leafy greens sit under a misting sprayer because lettuce is mostly water and wilts fast without high humidity.
segments.tr: Rau xanh lá nằm dưới máy phun sương vì rau diếp chủ yếu là nước và héo nhanh nếu không có độ ẩm cao.

segments.src: The bananas are a shelf apart from the apples for a reason: apples give off **ethylene**, a natural ripening gas, and it would turn your green bananas brown ahead of schedule.
segments.tr: Chuối cách xa táo một kệ vì lý do: táo tỏa ra **ethylene**, một loại khí chín tự nhiên, và nó sẽ biến chuối xanh của bạn thành nâu trước thời hạn.

segments.src: That same ethylene is a kitchen trick — put an unripe avocado in a paper bag with an apple and it ripens in a day or two because the gas gets trapped around it.
segments.tr: Ethylene tương tự đó là một mẹo nhà bếp — đặt quả bơ chưa chín vào túi giấy với một quả táo và nó sẽ chín trong một hoặc hai ngày vì khí bị mắc kẹt xung quanh nó.

segments.src: And that whole chilled journey from a California field to a Chicago shelf has a name: the **cold chain**.
segments.tr: Và toàn bộ hành trình làm lạnh đó từ một cánh đồng California đến kệ Chicago có tên: **chuỗi lạnh**.

segments.src: Every truck, warehouse, and display case is refrigerated so the produce never warms up and restarts its clock.
segments.tr: Mỗi xe tải, kho, và tủ trưng bày đều được làm lạnh để sản phẩm không bao giờ nóng lên và khởi động lại chu kỳ lão hóa.

segments.src: When one link breaks — a truck's cooler fails for a few hours — you see it days later as mushy strawberries.
segments.tr: Khi một liên kết bị gãy — bộ làm lạnh của xe tải bị hỏng vài tiếng — bạn sẽ thấy nó vài ngày sau là dâu tây mềm nhũn.

segments.src: In the U.S., roughly a third of food is lost or wasted, and a big share of the produce portion traces back to breaks in exactly this chain.
segments.tr: Ở Hoa Kỳ, khoảng một phần ba thực phẩm bị mất hoặc lãng phí, và một phần lớn phần sản phẩm có thể quy về những gián đoạn trong chính chuỗi này.

segments.src: ## 📚 Today's Terms
segments.tr: ## 📚 Các Thuật Ngữ Hôm Nay

segments.src: - **Respiration:** The process by which harvested produce burns its stored sugars, giving off heat, CO2, and water — the main driver of aging after picking.
segments.tr: - **Hô hấp:** Quá trình mà sản phẩm thu hoạch đốt cháy đường lưu trữ của nó, tỏa ra nhiệt, CO2, và nước — động lực chính của lão hóa sau khi hái.

segments.src: - **Cold chain:** An unbroken series of refrigerated steps (harvest, transport, storage, display) that keeps produce cold from farm to consumer.
segments.tr: - **Chuỗi lạnh:** Một loạt các bước làm lạnh không bị gãy (thu hoạch, vận chuyển, lưu trữ, trưng bày) giữ sản phẩm lạnh từ trang trại đến người tiêu dùng.

segments.src: - **Ethylene:** A natural plant gas that triggers ripening; useful for ripening on purpose but harmful when it over-ripens nearby produce.
segments.tr: - **Ethylene:** Một loại khí thực vật tự nhiên kích hoạt sự chín; hữu ích để chín có chủ đích nhưng có hại khi nó làm chín quá sản phẩm gần đó.

segments.src: - **Chilling injury:** Damage to warm-climate crops stored too cold (below about 50°F/10°C), showing up as pitting, watery spots, and off-flavors.
segments.tr: - **Tổn thương do lạnh:** Tổn hại cho cây trồng khí hậu ấm được lưu trữ quá lạnh (dưới khoảng 50°F/10°C), xuất hiện dưới dạng chỏm lõm, vết ướt, và mất vị.

segments.src: - **Controlled-atmosphere storage:** Storage that lowers oxygen and raises carbon dioxide to slow ripening, letting crops like apples keep for months.
segments.tr: - **Kho lưu trữ có khí quyển kiểm soát:** Lưu trữ giảm oxy và tăng carbon dioxide để làm chậm sự chín, cho phép cây trồng như táo giữ được trong nhiều tháng.

segments.src: *Answers: 1) B — cold slows the respiration rate, so the produce ages and breaks down more slowly (it does not sterilize or rehydrate the food).
segments.tr: *Câu trả lời: 1) B — lạnh làm chậm tốc độ hô hấp, vì vậy sản phẩm lão hóa và phân hủy chậm hơn (nó không khử trùng hoặc tái hydrate thực phẩm).

segments.src: 2) False — apples release ethylene, which speeds ripening and turns bananas brown faster, so keep them apart.
segments.tr: 2) Sai — táo phát hành ethylene, giúp chín nhanh hơn và biến chuối thành nâu nhanh hơn, vì vậy giữ chúng cách xa.

segments.src: 3) C — the tomato is a warm-climate crop prone to chilling injury; apples, carrots, and cabbage tolerate near-freezing storage well.*
segments.tr: 3) C — cà chua là một cây trồng khí hậu ấm dễ bị tổn thương do lạnh; táo, cà rốt, và bắp cải chịu được lưu trữ gần đóng băng tốt.*
